content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni with cheese and frankfurters (or hot dogs) is a dish made of boiled pasta tossed in melted processed cheese and mixed with sliced cooked sausages or hot dogs. It is popular as a quick lunch or snack, especially among children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century as an easy, nutritious school lunch.
The combination of pasta and processed cheese provides a fast source of carbs and protein.
In Russia a similar ready‑to‑eat version is often called “macaroni for kids”.
Sausages can be plain boiled or smoked, changing the flavor profile.
Processed cheese often contains emulsifiers that keep the sauce smooth when heated.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The dish quickly replenishes glucose stores, useful for physical activity or growth periods in children.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Sausages and cheese provide animal protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Processed cheese contributes calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Sausages and cheese supply B1, B2, B12 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible carbs
items.content: Wheat pasta is quickly digested, delivering rapid energy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Both sausages and processed cheese often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Processed cheese and some sausages are rich in saturated fats, which in excess may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Ready‑made mixes may include flavor enhancers, emulsifiers, and stabilizers that are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy should avoid processed cheese.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the macaroni until al dente, drain, add the processed cheese and stir until a smooth sauce forms. Finally, fold in sliced pre‑cooked frankfurters or hot dogs. Serve hot, optionally garnished with herbs or crunchy croutons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days in an airtight container. Keep dry pasta and cheese blocks in a cool, dry place, and opened sausage packages in the fridge.
